title: Import raw files
doc: Recognises each vendor file set with the reader that accepts it and checks it against the limits of the platform; it changes nothing.

title: Convert to mzML
doc: Writes the spectra of each sample as mzML; the version of this step names the writer.

peaks.title: Peaks
peaks.description: file: the points the file holds (the centroids of the maker where it has them, else the profile, which the next step reduces to peaks and the run reports); profile: the profile points of the file, an error where it has none; mzlab: our own centroids, with parameters estimated on the sample and written in the mzML (MS:1000035)

zlib_level.title: Compression level
zlib_level.description: zlib level of the binary arrays, 0 (none) to 9 (smallest)

numpress.title: MS-Numpress
numpress.description: Lossy MS-Numpress linear prediction of m/z and short logged float of intensities, smaller files

dad.title: Optical detector
dad.description: Also write the UV / PDA matrix of the sample as MS:1000804 spectra (one per instant, wavelengths in nm) after the scans; off: the file is the one written without the option

title: Build scan index
doc: Reads the scans of each sample once and writes the .mzidx the later steps read in slices.

budget.title: Working memory
budget.description: Bytes of peaks held in memory while the index is built; the rest goes to a scratch file and the bytes of the index do not change

title: Estimate parameters
doc: Measures the noise floor, the m/z tolerance, the peak width and the dead time of each file from its own data and writes the proofs; it proposes values, the next step decides.

title: Detect features
doc: Finds the chromatographic peaks of the MS1 scans of each file, with their quality, isotopologues and families. The parameters are common to every algorithm; each algorithm adds its own.

floor.title: Noise floor
floor.description: Points below are ignored; left empty, it is estimated from the intensity histogram

rt_range.title: RT range
rt_range.description: Optional [min, max]: only rows eluting inside are kept, for every file; left empty, all rows

mass_defect.title: Mass defect
mass_defect.description: Unit axis only: fractional part of m/z where the strong peaks pile up; measured on the file when left empty

long_trace.title: Long trace
long_trace.description: A trace longer than this is background and is not taken

merge_overlap.title: Merge overlap
merge_overlap.description: Rows within the mass tolerance are one ion when their scans overlap by this share of the shorter trace

min_width.title: Minimum width
min_width.description: Drops features narrower than this share of the typical peak width of the file; 0 = off

min_snr.title: Minimum S/N
min_snr.description: A feature whose apex is below this many times the noise of its flanks is dropped; 0 = off

isotopes.title: Isotope grouping
isotopes.description: averagine tests the ratios natural abundance allows; grouper is the isotope grouper of mzmine, with no ratio test

iso_ppm.title: Isotope m/z tolerance
iso_ppm.description: grouper only: m/z tolerance of an isotope step, the larger of this and the absolute one

iso_abs_da.title: Isotope absolute tolerance
iso_abs_da.description: grouper only: absolute lower bound of the m/z tolerance

iso_rt_tol.title: Isotope RT tolerance
iso_rt_tol.description: grouper only: largest RT distance of an isotopologue to the start row

iso_max_charge.title: Isotope largest charge
iso_max_charge.description: grouper only: the charges tried, from 1 up to this

iso_monotonic.title: Only heavier isotopes
iso_monotonic.description: grouper only: look only above the start row

iso_representative.title: Group representative
iso_representative.description: grouper only: the row of a group that is not marked as an isotopologue

algorithms.title: Mass traces
algorithms.doc: Builds mass traces scan by scan and cuts them at the minima; defaults and fields of trace::Params in crates/mzlab-feat/src/trace.rs.

algorithms.title: CentWave
algorithms.doc: Regions of interest in m/z, then a continuous wavelet transform over the expected peak widths.

references.note: CentWave: ROI detection and the wavelet peak model

applicability.note: High resolution centroided data with a known range of peak widths

broad_peaks.title: Broad peaks
broad_peaks.description: Also looks for bands 30-300 s wide (overloaded or interconverting compounds) that the narrow peaks leave out; a band is marked, and the filter against the blank can judge it

algorithms.title: ADAP and local minimum
algorithms.doc: The detection of mzmine 3: mass detection, ADAP chromatograms, optional Savitzky-Golay smoothing, then the local-minimum resolver. floor is the noise and the group intensity, min_height the highest point and the peak height, min_points the consecutive scans; the trace parameters max_gap, long_trace and merge_overlap do not apply.

references.note: MZmine 3: mass detection and the local-minimum resolver

applicability.note: High resolution centroided data, as mzmine expects

noise_factor.title: Factor of lowest signal
noise_factor.description: A point below this many times the lowest signal of its scan is not taken; 0 = the noise floor

smooth_window.title: Smoothing window
smooth_window.description: Savitzky-Golay window before the minimum search, 0 for none; height and area stay those of the raw trace.

algorithms.title: Threshold and derivative
algorithms.doc: Smooths each extracted chromatogram and keeps the apexes where the first derivative changes sign above the floor; fits unit resolution and few points per peak.

applicability.note: Unit resolution full scan or MRM with few points per peak

lr.title: Unit resolution
lr.evidence: LR_FLOOR, LR_MIN_HEIGHT and LR_MIN_SNR of recipe_lr.rs; the preview proposes the values of each file; on profile scans the floor is the mode of the noise lump

title: Align features
doc: Groups the features of all the files into rows by m/z and RT and writes the aligned table. Today one call (series::align_and_fill) does this and the filling of the gaps.

mode.title: Rows
mode.description: One row per family of ions (isotopologues, adducts, in-source fragments) or one per ion

ppm.title: m/z tolerance
ppm.description: At unit resolution the engine reads a negative value as Da

tol_da.title: m/z tolerance (Da)
tol_da.description: Unit axis only; left empty, the recipe of the file (measured window or 0.35 Da)

rt_gap.title: RT gap
rt_gap.description: Largest gap of RT between neighbouring features of one row

split_gap.title: Split gap
split_gap.description: A row with two features of one file (close isomers) is cut at the RT gaps above this

rt_warp.title: RT correction
rt_warp.description: Brings the RT of every file to a common one before the features are grouped, from anchors (peaks every file shows) found by a coarse alignment: piecewise (medians by blocks), loess (local regression), ransac (a line robust to wrong anchors); off: the RT as the files give it

rt_coarse_gap.title: Coarse RT gap
rt_coarse_gap.description: RT gap of the coarse alignment that finds the anchors, and the widest spread of an anchor over the files: the drift between files the correction can follow

rt_span.title: LOESS span
rt_span.description: Fraction of the anchors each local fit takes (loess)

rt_inlier.title: RANSAC distance
rt_inlier.description: Largest distance of an anchor from the line to agree with it (ransac)

rt_seed.title: RANSAC seed
rt_seed.description: Seed of the random samples of the line (ransac); the same seed gives the same correction

weak_files.title: Weak tier files
weak_files.description: Features from 0.3 of the minimum height up are kept as rows only if this many files in a run show them; 0 = no weak tier

link_rt.title: Family link RT
link_rt.description: Family mode: largest RT distance between an ion and the root of its family in one file for the two rows to be joined

max_span.title: Family row span
max_span.description: Family mode: largest RT span of the groups joined in one row

min_dependent.title: Family link files
min_dependent.description: Family mode: an ion that is mostly the base of its own family joins a family only if it follows its root in this many files

algorithms.title: Groups by m/z and RT gaps
algorithms.doc: Groups the features of the files by m/z and by the RT gaps between neighbours, per family or per ion (`famalign`, `align`).

algorithms.title: Join aligner
algorithms.doc: The join aligner of mzmine 3: the file with the most features left gives the rows, each feature of the others goes to the best-scored row inside the tolerances. One row per ion whatever mode says; ppm is the m/z tolerance; rt_gap, max_ppm_span, drop_artefacts, split_gap, rt_warp and the family parameters do not apply.

references.note: MZmine 3: the join aligner and the peak finder

applicability.note: High resolution feature tables, as mzmine expects

rt_tol.title: RT tolerance
rt_tol.description: Half width of the RT range of a row

abs_da.title: Absolute m/z tolerance
abs_da.description: Lower bound of the m/z tolerance; the larger of it and ppm wins

title: Fill gaps
doc: Where a file shows no feature of a row, integrates its raw trace in the window of the row and marks the cell as filled.

ppm.title: m/z tolerance
ppm.description: At unit resolution the engine reads a negative value as Da

tol_da.title: m/z tolerance (Da)
tol_da.description: Unit axis only; left empty, the recipe of the file (measured window or 0.35 Da)

rt_tol.title: RT tolerance
rt_tol.description: Half width added to the window of RT

long_trace.title: Long trace
long_trace.description: A trace longer than this is background and is not taken

algorithms.title: Trace integration
algorithms.doc: Integrates the raw trace of the file in the window of the row at the noise floor (`gapfill`); the cell keeps an area only.

algorithms.title: Peak finder
algorithms.doc: The peak finder of mzmine 3: in the m/z and RT range of the row, the most intense point of each scan, then a peak around an interior apex while the shape stays within the intensity tolerance. floor is the noise of the mass list; max_gap and long_trace do not apply.

references.note: MZmine 3: the join aligner and the peak finder

applicability.note: High resolution centroided data, as mzmine expects

intensity_tol.title: Intensity tolerance
intensity_tol.description: A point joins the peak while it is not above its neighbour toward the apex by more than this fraction

abs_da.title: Absolute m/z tolerance
abs_da.description: Lower bound of the m/z tolerance; the larger of it and ppm wins

title: Filter table
doc: Keeps the rows that pass an ordered list of rules over the samples (campioni/2); blanks and dark files never count as samples, and a rule that cannot be evaluated is an error.

samples.title: Roles and times of the files

table.title: Table view with the rows kept

min_detected.title: Minimum files
min_detected.description: Peaks found by the detection in at least this many files that are not blanks; left empty, the rule is off

min_replicate_fraction.title: Minimum replicate fraction
min_replicate_fraction.description: A row is kept if, in at least one group of replicates (same series, role, time and concentration, or the same group when it is set), it is detected in at least this fraction of the files, rounded to a whole file and at least one; left empty, the rule is off
min_replicate_fraction.x-tip: Kept if some replicate group has the row detected in at least this fraction of its files.

min_area.title: Minimum area
min_area.description: The largest area over the files is at least this; left empty, the rule is off

min_height.title: Minimum height
min_height.description: The largest height over the files is at least this; left empty, the rule is off

blank_ratio.title: Sample to blank ratio
blank_ratio.description: The largest area of a sample is at least this many times the mean area of the blanks; needs a blank in the samples; left empty, the rule is off

blank_quantity.title: Blank quantity
blank_quantity.description: What is compared with the blank: area, height or normalised area; used with the sample to blank ratio only

blank_stat.title: Blank level
blank_stat.description: The blank level of a row: mean or maximum over the blank files (a blank without a peak counts as 0)

blank_scope.title: Blank comparison
blank_scope.description: max_feature judges the row by its best sample; each_feature keeps it only if every sample with a peak reaches the threshold

blank_cells.title: Blank cells
blank_cells.description: detected counts only the blank cells the detection found (a gap-filled or missing blank cell is 0, as in mzmine); all also counts the gap-filled blank cells, the behaviour of version 1
blank_cells.x-tip: Which blank cells set the blank level: only the detected ones, or the gap-filled ones too.

blank_subtract.title: Subtract the blank
blank_subtract.description: The view shows sample minus ratio times the blank level, not below 0, instead of only filtering; area or normalised area only; the ratio is at least 1 when any blank option is set

blank_match.title: Blank matching
blank_match.description: all compares every sample with all blanks; batch or matrix compares each sample only with the blanks of its batch or matrix (campioni/2 or /3), and a sample with none falls back to all blanks, listed per file in the counts as bianco_ripiego; not with the subtraction
blank_match.x-tip: Compare each sample only with the blanks of its batch or matrix; others use all blanks.

blank_keep_istd.title: Keep the internal standard
blank_keep_istd.description: The internal-standard row skips the blank rule, because it is spiked in the blanks too; needs the normalisation istd

qc_zero.title: Count missing QC as 0
qc_zero.description: The QC CV counts the QC files without a peak as 0 and the row needs no minimum of them; the series still needs the minimum number of qc files

qc_cv_max.title: Maximum QC CV
qc_cv_max.description: CV of the areas over the files with the role qc is at most this; a row needs a peak in at least the minimum number of them; fewer qc files than that is the error error.qc.tooFew; left empty, the rule is off

qc_min_files.title: Minimum QC files
qc_min_files.description: QC files with a peak that the row needs for the QC rule, and QC files that the series needs

dup_ppm.title: Duplicate m/z window
dup_ppm.description: Of the rows within this many ppm in m/z and the duplicate RT window of each other only the one with the largest area is kept; left empty, the rule is off

dup_da.title: Duplicate m/z window (Da)
dup_da.description: Unit axis only: of the rows within this many Da in m/z and the duplicate RT window of each other only the one with the largest area is kept; dup_ppm on a unit-resolution table is an error; left empty, the rule is off
dup_da.x-tip: Of rows this many Da apart in m/z and close in RT, only the strongest is kept.

dup_rt.title: Duplicate RT window
dup_rt.description: RT distance under which two rows may be duplicates; used with the duplicate m/z window only

require_ms2.title: Require MS2
require_ms2.description: An MS2 is linked to the peak; left empty, the rule is off

normalize.title: Normalisation
normalize.description: Scale of the areas of each file: total area or median area
normalize.x-tip: Scale each file by its total area, its median area or the area of the internal standard.

istd_id.title: Internal standard row
istd_id.description: Id of the row of the internal standard; used with the normalisation istd

istd_mz.title: Internal standard m/z
istd_mz.description: m/z of the internal standard, with its RT: the nearest row (5 ppm, 0.2 min) is the standard; used with the normalisation istd when no row id is set
istd_mz.x-tip: m/z of the internal standard; with its RT, the nearest row is the standard.

istd_rt.title: Internal standard RT
istd_rt.description: RT of the internal standard; used with its m/z

title: Correct drift
doc: Brings the areas of each batch to the level of the QC files along the order of injection; refused with fewer than 5 QC files in a batch or QC files that are not at the start and the end of it. The measured areas are never overwritten.

samples.title: Roles and injection order of the files

table.title: Table view with a factor for every cell

method.title: Curve
method.description: Line or local line (LOESS) through the areas of the QC files of each batch, against the position of the injection

span.title: LOESS span
span.description: Share of the QC files of a batch in the neighbourhood of each fit; used by the local line only

title: Group ions
doc: Groups the rows of a per-ion table that are one compound: same RT, heights that correlate over the files, then isotope steps and ion species that give one neutral mass. Every row stays, with a group id; the edges can go to a molecular network.

references.note: Ion identity molecular networking: ion species of one molecule linked by peak correlation; the edge columns of GNPS
CAMERA: grouping by apex within a share of the FWHM and by correlation, isotopes and adducts by mass difference

polarity.title: Polarity
polarity.description: Which list of ion species is searched; auto = the polarity of the files of the table

ions_pos.title: Positive ion species
ions_pos.description: Comma-separated species searched in positive mode, among [M+H]+ [M+Na]+ [M+NH4]+ [M+K]+ [M+H-H2O]+ [M+H-2H2O]+ [M+2H]2+ [M+H+Na]2+ [2M+H]+ [2M+Na]+ [2M+NH4]+

ions_neg.title: Negative ion species
ions_neg.description: Comma-separated species searched in negative mode, among [M-H]- [M+Cl]- [M+HCOO]- [M+CH3COO]- [M-H-H2O]- [M-2H]2- [2M-H]- [2M+HCOO]-

rt_tol.title: RT tolerance
rt_tol.description: Largest distance between the RT of two rows of one compound

apex_fwhm.title: Apex distance
apex_fwhm.description: Largest apex distance in the shared files, as a share of the wider peak width (CAMERA perfwhm)

min_corr.title: Height correlation
min_corr.description: Smallest Pearson correlation of the heights of two rows over the files (CAMERA cor_eic_th)

min_corr_samples.title: Files for the correlation
min_corr_samples.description: The heights are compared only when both rows are measured in at least this many files

mz_abs.title: Smallest m/z tolerance
mz_abs.description: Floor of the m/z tolerance at low mass

max_charge.title: Largest charge
max_charge.description: Largest charge an isotope step is read with

title: Compare conditions
doc: Welch's t on log2(area + pseudocount) for each comparison of the design and a one-way ANOVA over all the conditions, with Benjamini-Hochberg q-values and log2FC; refused with a reason and no number when a condition has fewer than 3 files. The p-values stay in this output: no view shows them.

report.title: Tests per comparison, ANOVA and heat map data (stat/1)

pseudocount.title: Pseudocount
pseudocount.description: Added to every area before the logarithm and in the log2FC; without a value it is 3 x the median of the positive areas of the blanks, else of the reference, else the floor

floor.title: Pseudocount floor
floor.description: Smallest estimated pseudocount, and the one used when no file gives a noise level

title: Explore with PCA
doc: Principal components of the samples after the blank filter, the imputation and the scaling, with the variance explained and the stability of the loadings leaving one sample out; refused under 5 samples. A view: it tests nothing.

report.title: Scores, loadings, explained variance, stability and ellipses

factor.title: Blank factor
factor.description: A feature must exceed the blank level times this factor; skipped when no file is a blank

stat.title: Blank level
stat.description: Level of the blank files: the maximum or the mean of their areas

min_detect.title: Files above the blank
min_detect.description: Sample files that must exceed the blank threshold

min_intensity.title: Minimum area
min_intensity.description: Smallest maximum area of a feature, and the area that counts as present

min_samples.title: Minimum samples present
min_samples.description: Samples in which a feature must be present

transform.title: Transform
transform.description: log2 of the areas after the imputation, or the areas as they are

scaling.title: Scaling
scaling.description: Pareto divides by the square root of the sd; auto divides by the sd and inflates the noise with few samples

ncomp.title: Components
ncomp.description: Components kept in scores and loadings

title: Kendrick mass defect
doc: KM and KMD of every ion and the series of ions that share the KMD, with their members, steps and retention trend. A series is a candidate with its evidence, never an identification.

report.title: Kendrick values per ion and the candidate series

tol_mda.title: KMD window
tol_mda.description: Width of the KMD window of a series

min_members.title: Minimum members
min_members.description: Distinct nominal Kendrick masses a series needs

title: Plausibility of the values
doc: Seven checks of the numbers the table shows: finite values, m/z and RT inside a real run, no negative area or height, a width and an apex for every detected peak, rows with no peak in any file and the ppm error of the identity columns. Numbers only: a flagged row is a value to look at, never a verdict.

mz_min.title: Lowest m/z
mz_min.description: A row below it is flagged: no LC-MS run reads there

mz_max.title: Highest m/z
mz_max.description: A row above it is flagged

rt_max.title: Longest run
rt_max.description: A row with an RT outside 0 and this value is flagged: check the unit of the times

width_max.title: Widest peak
width_max.description: A detected peak wider than this, or with no width or apex, is flagged

ppm_max.title: Largest ppm error
ppm_max.description: A row whose m/z is further than this from its neutral mass plus adduct is flagged; read only in a high-resolution table

mz_tol_da.title: Alignment tolerance
mz_tol_da.description: 0.1 Da or more is unit resolution and the ppm error is not read; without a value the recipe stored in the table decides

title: Link MS2 scans
doc: Attaches to each peak the MS2 scans whose precursor lies in the peak and in the isolation window, with the purity of the precursor. Today this runs inside `features.detect` (one pass over the index), so it has no executor of its own: taking it out would change the bytes of the feature files.

default_half_window.title: Default isolation half window
default_half_window.description: Used when the index records no isolation window; the peak is then marked as estimated

tol_ppm.title: m/z tolerance
tol_ppm.description: Window of the peak in the MS1 scan of the precursor; at unit resolution the engine reads a negative value as Da

tol_da.title: m/z tolerance (Da)
tol_da.description: Unit axis only; left empty, the recipe of the file (measured window or 0.35 Da)

weak.title: Weak purity
weak.description: Purity below which an MS2 is weak evidence; it is not dropped

margin_s.title: Trigger margin
margin_s.description: Seconds added on each side of the feature RT range to pair MS2 scans, 0 meaning one MS1 cycle.

title: Export table as CSV
doc: Writes the feature table, under the view of the filter step when one is wired, as a CSV file; the column names carry the file names, so equal names give equal bytes.

samples.title: Roles and times of the files

kind.title: Format
kind.description: full: one row per feature with the summaries; full_mzmine: the same with the words of mzmine for the filled and targeted cells; quant: the areas for FBMN; csv_semicolon: the sheet of features with ;

title: Export inclusion list
doc: Writes the m/z and RT windows of the expected products as a CSV in the columns of the inclusion list of mzFinder, sorted by RT; it adds no level and no verdict.

tp.title: Expected products with their RT (a JSON list, or the table of tp.link)

adducts.title: Adducts
adducts.description: Adducts of the ion table separated by commas, or a list of your own as a CSV with the header name;delta;charge;comment; one row per product and adduct; left empty it is [M-H]- for products linked in negative mode and [M+H]+ otherwise

rt_window.title: RT half window
rt_window.description: Each row spans the expected RT of the product plus and minus this; the start is never below 0

title: Export table as mzTab-M
doc: Writes the feature table, under the view of the filter step when one is wired, as an mzTab-M 2.0 file: one small molecule and one feature per row, areas per file and per group, and an evidence for a row whose identity names a hypothesis. Every row is reliability 4 (unknown compound): the export adds no identity and raises no level.

samples.title: Roles and times of the files
